name: Complete Septate Uterus

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) Classification Criteria

criteria.description: Visualization of a fibrous or muscular septum dividing the uterine cavity completely on imaging or surgery
Normal external uterine contour without fundal indentation or cleft
Presence of reproductive complications such as recurrent pregnancy loss or infertility

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a complete uterine cavity septum with normal external uterine contour confirmed by imaging or surgery
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is typically confirmed by 3D ultrasound, MRI, or hysteroscopy combined with laparoscopy

searchTerms: loss of pregnancy in early weeks

common.notes: Painful menstruation reported in some cases
Increased risk due to uterine anomaly

occasional.notes: Heavy menstrual bleeding in some patients

searchTerms: pelvic pain not linked to periods
chronic pelvic pain unrelated to cycle

rare.symptomName: Asherman syndrome secondary to surgical intervention

searchTerms: abnormal uterus with endometrial tissue outside

imaging: 3D transvaginal ultrasound showing complete uterine cavity septum with normal external contour
MRI pelvis confirming septate uterus anatomy
Hysterosalpingography demonstrating division of uterine cavity
other: Hysteroscopic visualization of fibrous or muscular septum
Laparoscopic confirmation of normal external uterine contour

distinguishingFeatures: External uterine contour shows fundal cleft or indentation
Two separate uterine horns with a wide angle between them
Often associated with a single or double cervix
Normal uterine cavity with a concave fundal contour
Typically asymptomatic and considered a normal variant

redFlags: Recurrent pregnancy loss without other identifiable cause
Severe infertility despite normal ovarian function
Preterm labor or malpresentation in pregnancy
references: American Society for Reproductive Medicine. The ASRM classification of female genital tract anomalies. Fertil Steril. 2021.
Grimbizis GF, et al. The ESHRE/ESGE consensus on the classification of female genital tract congenital anomalies. Hum Reprod. 2013.
Chan YY, et al. Reproductive outcomes in women with congenital uterine anomalies: a systematic review. Ultrasound Obstet Gynecol. 2011.
